guide.title: This is a sample matter
guide.intro: Everything in it is fictional: an I-601A provisional waiver for a Guatemalan husband of a U.S. citizen, with 14 scanned documents marked SPECIMEN. Some documents and answers are missing on purpose.
guide.try: Press Review documents first. In about 5 to 10 minutes Claude lists what's there, what's missing, and what to ask the client for. Then compare it with the list this card shows.
caught: No proof the immigrant visa fee was paid. NVC's letter asks for it, and neither intake confirms it.
No proof of the wife's U.S. citizenship.
No English translation of the Guatemalan birth certificate.
The wife hasn't said whether she would stay or move, so hardship has to be argued both ways until she decides.
No diagnosis or therapy records for the son's autism, the core of the hardship case.
No court record of the 2019 DWI arrest. A class certificate isn't a disposition, and the outcome decides whether it's a conviction.
The intake doesn't say whether he has left the U.S. since 2012 (his mother died in Guatemala in 2014). A return after a year of unlawful presence would be a permanent bar the I-601A can't waive.
His intake gives the wedding date as March 12, 2016; the certificate says March 19, 2016.
guide.after: A full build of the packet takes about an hour and uses your Claude plan like any matter. Archive this matter when you're done with it.
